name: print()
desc: Displays output on the screen. The first function every Pythonista learns.

name: input()
desc: Reads a line of text from the user. Always returns a string.

name: len()
desc: Returns the number of items in a string, list, tuple, dict or set.

name: type()
desc: Returns the type of an object — int, str, list, and friends.

name: range()
desc: Generates a sequence of numbers. The backbone of for loops.

name: enumerate()
desc: Loop with automatic index counting. Cleaner than range(len(...)).
example:
for i, fruit in enumerate(["a", "b"]):
    print(i, fruit)  # 0 a / 1 b

name: zip()
desc: Pairs up items from multiple iterables, stopping at the shortest.
example:
for name, age in zip(["A", "B"], [20, 21]):
    print(name, age)

name: sorted()
desc: Returns a new sorted list, leaving the original untouched.

name: sum() / min() / max()
desc: Quick stats over any iterable of numbers.

name: abs() / round() / pow()
desc: Everyday math helpers.

name: int() / float() / str() / bool()
desc: Convert between types. Essential after input(), which returns strings.

name: list() / dict() / set() / tuple()
desc: Build the four core containers, or convert between them.

name: upper() / lower()
desc: Change case. Great for normalising user input before comparing.

name: strip()
desc: Removes whitespace (or given characters) from both ends.

name: split() / join()
desc: Break a string apart, or glue a list together. Two sides of one coin.

name: replace()
desc: Swap every occurrence of a substring. Strings are immutable — this returns a new one.

name: find()
desc: Index of the first match, or -1 when absent. Use 'in' for a simple check.

name: startswith() / endswith()
desc: Clean True/False checks for prefixes and suffixes.

name: append() / extend()
desc: append adds one item; extend adds every item of another iterable.

name: insert() / remove() / pop()
desc: insert at a position, remove by value, pop by index (returns the item).
example:
a = [1, 2, 3]
a.pop()     # 3, a is now [1, 2]
a.remove(1)   # a is now [2]

name: sort() / reverse()
desc: Sort or reverse in place (unlike sorted(), which returns a new list).

name: index() / count()
desc: Find where an item lives, or how many times it appears.

name: get()
desc: Safe lookup — returns default instead of crashing on missing keys.

name: keys() / values() / items()
desc: Views over a dict's keys, values, or (key, value) pairs. items() powers for-loops.
example:
for k, v in {"a": 1}.items():
    print(k, v)  # a 1

name: update()
desc: Merge another dict in, overwriting clashes.

name: if / elif / else
desc: Branch your logic. elif chains keep nested ifs flat.

name: for
desc: Loop over anything iterable — lists, strings, dicts, ranges.

name: while
desc: Loop until a condition flips. Remember to change something inside, or it never ends.

name: def / return
desc: Define reusable functions. return hands a value back to the caller.

name: try / except
desc: Handle errors gracefully instead of crashing.

name: with (files)
desc: The safe way to work with files — auto-closes, even on errors.

name: lambda
desc: Tiny anonymous functions for one-liners, e.g. with sorted().

name: list comprehension
syntax: [expr for x in it if cond]
desc: Build lists in one expressive line. Very Pythonic.
example:
[x*x for x in range(6) if x % 2 == 0]
# [0, 4, 16]
